qualified_claims: The actual RibaMod run reproduces the complete qualified DUMMY-20H active-River day-1 accepted-state prefix, including t=24 level 1.000007990372381 m and storage excess 7.990372381083688 m3.
The first post-boundary MF6 River solve publishes 8.000042512172085 m3/day back to Ribasim, matching the prospectively frozen DUMMY-20H6 current-forcing reference within numerical precision.
Actual Ribasim allocation output contains distinct t=0 and t=24 records.
The actual t=24 UserDemand allocation is 39.99037238105666 m3/day root and 0 external, matching the DUMMY-20H6 free-alpha oracle.
The t=24 root-allocation increase above the t=0 32 m3/day allocation is 7.99037238105666 m3/day, equal within numerical precision to the accepted day-1 Basin storage excess.

The actual pinned product therefore carries accepted physical storage memory into the next management boundary while current active-River forcing remains separately forecast-attenuable under the tested allocation topology.
External physical supply remains zero through the first post-boundary segment and the coupled physical ledger closes at reported numerical precision.

coupling_contract.physical_window: Active River forcing is realized reciprocally and changes accepted Basin state during day 1.
coupling_contract.accepted_memory: The resulting accepted storage excess is retained as management-visible memory at t=24.
coupling_contract.current_forcing: The next active-River forcing is physically present at the same management boundary but is not equivalent to accepted memory.
coupling_contract.allocation_forecast: For the tested topology, the actual t=24 allocation equals Q_source + accepted_memory, consistent with the H6 free-alpha solution that attenuates the current implicit negative forcing.
coupling_contract.realization: The new allocation governs only subsequent physical realization; it does not retroactively alter day-1.

boundaries: The low_storage_factor itself is not exposed as an actual RibaMod XMI variable in this test; the product bridge is qualified by the preregistered allocation-output equivalence to the H6 oracle, not by inventing direct alpha observability.
The result applies to the tested single-Basin active-River/UserDemand/LevelDemand topology and exact pinned product versions.
No claim of arbitrary Ribasim network allocation equivalence.
No implicit same-window coupled fixed point is established.
No production SWAP5 admission, storage-partition decision or drainage-ownership decision.
downstream: Use H7 as the end-to-end authority for the accepted-memory/current-forcing separation. Any further work should vary topology, priority, forcing direction or temporal regime rather than re-prove this same single-Basin case.
